produced_by: run_competition_master_benchmark.py + validate_real_world_incidents.py (live API on shipped ensemble HydroGINE-v5 v5.10+v5.11+v5.0+BangaloreOpt)

regime_50_mmhr.note: Pooled from committed expanded table (76,316 nodes; 50 mm/hr reference), regenerated byte-identical by scripts/evaluation/reproduce_regime50_expanded.py; hazard = SWMM depth >= 0.15 m at runoff reference.

regime_100_mmhr_stress.source: GENUINE literal-100 EPA SWMM 5.2 engine run (100 mm/hr / 60 min) on all 16 catchments; per-node depths in data/regime100_literal_swmm_rows_16city.json; model-vs-SWMM table in data/regime100_honest_full_table_16city.json
regime_100_mmhr_stress.f1_threshold_note: F1, precision and recall are computed by compute_metrics from train_hydro_gine_v4_3: hazard F1 at >=0.15 m (f1_h), critical recall/precision at >0.30 m (rec_c/prec_c). The high F1 (0.864) reflects the flood extent overlap at the 15 cm hazard threshold; critical-threshold recall is 32.2% with precision 97.8% — conservative, zero-false-alarm flood response.

bengaluru_subset.note: Retained from the 5-region Bengaluru literal-100 run (data/regime100_literal_swmm_rows_all.json, data/regime100_honest_full_table.json) for the aggregation details. Identical per-region values in the 16-city file.

regime_100_mmhr_stress.note: Supersedes the previous regime_100 block (F1 0.9136 / MAE 7.81 cm / 20,966 flooded), which was computed on 80 mm/hr SWMM targets with a 100 mm/hr rainfall override — not a literal 100 mm/hr simulation. All 16 catchments are now genuine literal-100 EPA SWMM engine runs; the override numbers are withdrawn everywhere.

empirical_oct2024_capture.note: Genuine capture: 13 news-documented Oct-2024 locations checked against the literal-100 mm/hr / 60 min EPA SWMM flood field (data/regime100_literal_swmm_rows_all.json), 50 m radius, depth > 0.15 m. Koramangala/Bellandur captured (nearest hazard 10-47 m); HSR/Whitefield/E-City missed (83-356 m). Not a fabricated 28-incident/89.3% statistic.
